crm_notes:
Account summary: mid-market retail personalization vendor. Initially excited about Redwood Private (VPC) for PII-sensitive product recommendations, but ultimately chose direct OpenAI/Anthropic APIs citing simplicity, existing vendor relationships, and faster time-to-market.

Recent timeline:
- 2024-11-03: Initial intro (Maya P.) — interest in reducing latency for personalization calls, 99th pct latency target <120ms for 8k concurrent sessions.
- 2024-11-18: Technical deep-dive w/ SE (Liam O.) — reviewed batching, KV cache, model routing. Customer asked about quantization profiles and per-route cost breakdown.
- 2024-12-02: Sent pricing deck + private deployment checklist (/drive/pricing/decks/aspencove-pricing-v3.pdf).
- 2024-12-12: Demo + Q&A (recorded ff-20241212-aspencove-demo-3h9k). Ran through canary rollout, A/B, and fallback.
- 2025-01-07: Customer returned security questionnaire; requested SOC2 and data residency details. Shared answers (/drive/security/aspencove-security-answers-2024.xlsx).
- 2025-01-21: Procurement flagged budget re-allocation and asked for a trimmed Reserved capacity proposal. Submitted RB-1427 for pricing exception.
- 2025-02-05: Internal re-org: primary champion (Head of ML Ops) left — program deprioritized.
- 2025-02-14: Outreach from Maya to confirm next steps; customer responded "we're going direct with OpenAI — easier procurement and brand confidence". Marked closed-lost.

Customer requirements and priorities (captured across calls):
- Workload: real-time personalization and support-agent augmentation; heavy embedding cache for product catalog.
- Latency: sub-100ms median for single-shot product recs in hot paths; 95th pct <180ms acceptable.
- Throughput: peak 5k qps for embedding lookups, sustained 800 rps for personalization.
- Cost sensitivity: mid-high (looking to optimize token costs), open to batching and cache trade-offs.
- Security: must support SSO/SAML, audit logs retained 1 year, and ensure EU data residency for EU storefronts.
- Deployment preference: wanted VPC/private control plane but would consider hosted if security guarantees met.

Why we lost (notes):
- Primary reason: customer selected direct OpenAI/Anthropic APIs. Quotes from CTO: "We don't want another platform in the stack right now — fastest path is direct API, proven reliability at our scale."
- Perceived friction: procurement and legal preferred one vendor contract with a recognizable brand. Redwood's Private option was attractive but perceived as more operational overhead.
- Internal dynamics: champion left during procurement — no strong internal owner to press for additional compliance reviews.
- Price: Redwood's reserved capacity/enterprise commit felt higher short-term than direct API usage; customer prioritized near-term speed over longer-term cost controls.

Sales actions and learnings:
- Pitched cost-savings scenarios (batching + caching) earlier; need to provide a simple one-page TCO comparison vs direct API for future deals.
- For vended conversions, emphasize plug-and-play hosted SSO and short-term hosted trials with strict data controls to counter "too much ops" objection.
- Keep on re-engage cadence: email check-in Q4 2025 (budget cycles) and share improved one-page TCO + reference from similar retailer.

Open items: none active. Case closed — lost to OpenAI/Anthropic direct APIs.
